analyzed_vuln.description: `iloc_box_read` allocates `GF_ItemLocationEntry` with `gf_malloc` but does not initialize it before adding it to `ptr->location_entries`. If parsing later fails (e.g., due to truncated/invalid box size), cleanup runs via `gf_isom_box_del -> iloc_box_del -> iloc_entry_del`, which unconditionally calls `gf_list_count(location->extent_entries)`. Because `extent_entries` was never initialized, this becomes a wild pointer dereference and crashes in `gf_list_count`. Crash site is `gf_list_count`, but root cause is uninitialized `location_entry` state in `iloc_box_read` and unsafe destructor assumptions in `iloc_entry_del`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: From fuzz harness `fuzz_parse`, input is parsed as ISO boxes. A malformed/truncated `iloc` box (PoC has size 0 with type `iloc`) causes `iloc_box_read` to enter/partially process entries and then return error before `location_entry->extent_entries` is set. The partially built box is then freed on parse error, and `iloc_entry_del` dereferences the uninitialized `extent_entries` pointer, triggering SEGV.
